SMTO-LLM-0027 — The model server couldn't handle SMTO's tool instructions

GUID: 2d39a2fc-fe7f-414a-b30e-397c1c3e078a
Slug: tool-parser-rejected
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model server turned the request down with a message about how it reads the model's tool instructions. None of your tools ran and failed; nothing from this request was carried out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. If this small test also fails, the problem is in the server's setup for this model, not in your task.
  2. Send the copied error details to the person who manages the model server and ask them to check that its tool-call setting matches this model. SMTO needs the model to give tool instructions in a form the server can read, and only the server's setup can change that.
  3. After they confirm a fix, select Check saved model again, then on the stopped task, select Resume (or Continue task if that is what it shows). The rejected request ran none of your tools, so continuing is safe once the server reads tool instructions correctly.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model passes and the task continues without this error.

If it still fails

  • If the server can't be fixed soon, choose another model on the Main card, select Save Main, and start the remaining work as a new task, after checking what the stopped task already finished. Don't install extra software until the cause is confirmed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The provider rejected the request (HTTP 400/422) and its error text matched tool-parser markers ('tool parser', 'tool-call-parser', 'tool_call_parser') (tool_parser_rejected).

What this means

  • The rejection classifier found wording associated with the tool parser. This narrows the next check but does not prove the provider’s exact internal failure. Check the recorded status and serving configuration before changing the request or installing components.

Why this can happen

  • Provider diagnostic text matched the tool parser category. The exact rejected feature still needs confirmation.

How to diagnose it

  • Check that the serving model and selected native tool parser are compatible.
  • Have the provider operator reproduce the specific rejection with a small sanitized test, without sharing the original prompt or tool arguments.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the serving model and the server's native tool-call parser match (for example vLLM's --enable-auto-tool-choice with the --tool-call-parser for that model family). Correct the confirmed mismatch, verify with a small native tool-call request, then resume; the category comes from provider text markers and is not proof of the exact cause.
  • Check that the serving model and selected native tool parser are compatible. Ask the provider operator to correct the confirmed incompatibility before another Agent decision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The provider accepts a controlled request using the required native tool format.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The category is selected by bounded provider-text markers, not authoritative structured root-cause evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
